content.thinking: The monthly-spend-feature flag flipped from mixed to fully "on" at 07:16, right when the ZeroDivisionError errors began in spend_summary.py, pointing to the flag toggle as the likely cause. I already checked for deployments between 05:00 and 07:21 and found nothing, so now I want to narrow the window further to pinpoint what changed.

hypotheses.subject: monthly-spend-feature
hypotheses.summary: The monthly-spend-feature flag flipped from a partial rollout (35 off / 165 on) to fully on at 07:16:00Z, and the code path it enables (spend_summary.py) throws a ZeroDivisionError on every request that takes it, matching the fully-correlated jump in error_rate from ~1% baseline to ~30-35% starting exactly at that minute. No code or config deployment is recorded in the surrounding change window, latency and traffic are unaffected, and cpu_limit_cores stays flat at 3.0 throughout, ruling out resource/capacity causes.

supporting_evidence.claim: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47
error_rate jumps from 0.005 at 07:15:00Z to 0.34 at 07:16:00Z while p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, request_volume and cpu_used_cores/cpu_limit_cores remain in their prior ranges
cpu_limit_cores holds at 3.0 for every minute in the window, including the incident minutes

hypotheses.summary: If the flag evidence is set aside, the same symptom (ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py) could instead stem from a code change to that file that was not caught by the change-window queries already run; without further deploy history around 07:16 this can't be fully excluded.
